questions.q: What does a year-to-date (YTD) measure accumulate?
options: A running total from the start of the year through the current context, resetting to zero at the start of the next year
The total for the entire year, regardless of context
Only the current month's total
The average value across the whole year
questions.explain: YTD sums from January 1st (or the fiscal year start) up through whatever date is in context, then resets at the next year boundary.

questions.q: In a table broken out by month, what would TOTALYTD show for March?
options: The combined total of January, February, and March
Only March's own total
The average of January through March
The total for the entire year
questions.explain: TOTALYTD accumulates from the start of the year through the current row's date — so March's row includes everything from January through March.

questions.q: How does TOTALYTD's optional year_end_date parameter work?
options: You specify the last day of a fiscal year, and the 'year' boundary shifts to match it instead of December 31
It sets the exact date the measure should be evaluated for
It disables the year-to-date reset entirely
It only works when combined with DATEADD
questions.explain: Passing a value like "6/30" makes the fiscal year run from July 1 through June 30, instead of the default calendar year.

questions.q: What is TOTALYTD(<expr>, <dates>) exactly equivalent to?
options: CALCULATE(<expr>, DATESYTD(<dates>))
SUMX(<dates>, <expr>)
CALCULATE(<expr>, ALL(<dates>))
FILTER(<dates>, <expr>)
questions.explain: TOTALYTD is shorthand for wrapping DATESYTD's table of year-to-date dates in a CALCULATE — useful to know since DATESYTD is used directly in more flexible scenarios.

questions.q: What's the difference between TOTALMTD and TOTALQTD?
options: TOTALMTD resets monthly; TOTALQTD resets quarterly — otherwise they follow the same running-total pattern
TOTALMTD only works on measures; TOTALQTD only works on calculated columns
TOTALQTD requires a fiscal year end date; TOTALMTD does not
There is no difference — they are aliases for the same function
questions.explain: Both follow the identical accumulate-then-reset pattern as TOTALYTD, just on shorter cycles: monthly for TOTALMTD, quarterly for TOTALQTD.
